assignments.brief_reason: Using mirrored-pair contrast to judge violations more consistently across viewpoints matches applying the same moderation standard to both sides.
Stated open-mindedness/anti-bias attitude without a clear moderation removal rule or threat/toxicity standard.
Cursing and explicit hatred increase likelihood of not allowing/removing posts due to toxicity.
Foul language makes posts seem childish/rude and more removable, reflecting removal for vulgar/toxic tone.
Keeps strongly worded comments but removes mudslinging/cursing that detracts from meaningful discussion; closer to threat/toxicity exceptions than strict fairness across sides.
Focus on defending views without slinging; removal tied to disrespect/mudslinging rather than a consistent side-agnostic policy.
Explicitly rejects removing purely for political disagreement to preserve fairness across the paired sides.
Neutral checks for content that could be misconstrued as a call to violence or racist align with violence/racist exception logic.
Remove both posts if either uses foul/incendiary language, matching toxicity/vulgarity removal.
Keeps unless language is dehumanizing, racist, or promoting violence; removal for toxic/racist/violent content.
Pair comparison by sincerity/trolling (hate vs criticism) is not explicitly threat-based, but it filters out ragebait-like hateful content.
Checks vulgarity and whether it reads as opinions vs threats; partially maps to toxicity/threat-related removal.
Two-step flow: remove-worthy threatening language first; only then consider topic—fits violence/threat exception framing.
Denies posts using curse words/insults for lack of respectful discourse—removal for toxic/vulgar language.
No interpretable content provided ('none'), so it doesn’t map to a substantive moderation theme.
Remove posts that unfairly attack a demographic or are driven by hate, which is toxicity/hate removal.
Compare original vs mirror by core topic adherence and safety for consistency across the paired pair, aligning with same standard across both sides.
Internal affect/inflammation overriding agreement without a clear, specific keep/remove rule tied to threats/toxicity or side-agnostic moderation.
Remove name-calling/personal insults and egregious profanity—classic toxic/vulgarity removal cues.
Removal based on how ignorant/incendiary the content is; closer to exception criteria around inflammatory/inciting content than pure tone-vulgarity.
